Actor.description:
An opaque, transport-asserted caller identity.

Constructed by the transport after it authenticates the caller, relayed
verbatim by the kernel, and consumed only by plugins for data scoping. See
the [crate-level docs](crate) for the full contract.

claims.description:
Transport-asserted claims (e.g. `["admin"]`). Advisory only: the kernel
never branches on these. A plugin MAY consult them for its own
authorization decisions. Omitted from the wire when empty.

tenant_id.description:
Optional tenant / organization partition the user belongs to. Plugins
use it for multi-tenant data isolation. Omitted from the wire when
absent.

user_id.description:
Stable identifier for the authenticated user. Opaque to the kernel;
plugins use it to scope owned rows to a user.

ExecutionFence.description: Complete ownership envelope for one workflow execution generation.

queue_lease.description: Queue lease CAS identity. Direct execution may omit it.

repository.description:
Repository/ref reservation. Non-code workflows may omit it; coding
schedulers must require it before workspace preparation.

subject.description: Subject generation, absent only for a genuinely subjectless workflow.

workflow_generation.description:
Positive workflow generation. Reattachment keeps it; an intentional new
execution generation must increment it.

workflow_id.description: Stable workflow id. Recovery preserves this id.

FencedQueueEntry.description: One queue entry paired with its complete execution ownership fence.

execution.description: Exact generation and CAS lease ownership.

FencedQueueEntry.title: FencedQueueEntry

generation_fenced_leases_v1.description:
Supports `queue/v2/*`: monotonic subject/workflow/lease generations,
CAS renew/recovery/mutations, durable idempotency, and repository-ref
collision fencing.

max_lease_batch.description:
Maximum batch size accepted on [`METHOD_QUEUE_LEASE`]. Hosts clamp
requested `max` to this value.

priority_weighted.description:
`true` if the backend honors `priority` on `SubjectDispatch` (v0.5
reference implementation is strict FIFO within Pending status; later
backends may weight by priority).

expire_after_secs.description:
Optional grace window, in seconds, applied after `run_at`. If a
deferred entry is still pending past `run_at + expire_after_secs`
(e.g. the daemon was down through its window), the plugin drops it
on its next sweep instead of dispatching late. `None` means never
expire — always fire late whenever the daemon next leases. Ignored
when `run_at` is `None`.

run_at.description:
Optional RFC 3339 earliest-dispatch time. When set and in the
future, the entry is enqueued as deferred: it stays in
[`status::PENDING`] but is excluded from [`METHOD_QUEUE_LEASE`]
until this instant passes. `None` means dispatch as soon as
capacity allows (today's behavior).

enqueued.description:
`true` if a new entry was created. For immediate (non-deferred)
enqueues this stays idempotent: `false` if the dispatch was
rejected as a duplicate of an existing pending/assigned entry.
Deferred enqueues (`run_at` set) are always created — scheduling
the same subject for distinct times is legitimate — so `enqueued`
is `true` and any collision is surfaced via `warning` instead.

entry_id.description:
Stable entry id assigned by the plugin. Used by all subsequent
mutation calls.

subject_id.description: Convenience: the subject id from the dispatch envelope.

warning.description:
Non-fatal advisory. Set when the enqueue succeeded but the caller
may want to reconsider — most commonly that another pending,
deferred, or assigned entry already exists for this subject. The
duplicate is still enqueued; the caller (agent or operator) decides
whether to drop it. `None` when there is nothing to flag.

QueueEnqueueV2Request.description: Enqueue request for the generation-fenced scheduler.

idempotency_key.description:
Stable producer idempotency key (for example a GitHub delivery id plus
trigger id). Repeating a key returns the original entry and generation.

repository.description:
Exact repository/head-ref reservation for coding work. Non-code queue
entries may omit it.

QueueEnqueueV2Request.title: QueueEnqueueV2Request

QueueEnqueueV2Response.description:
Enqueue response carrying the immutable subject generation allocated to the
entry.

enqueued.description: `true` when this call created the entry; `false` for an idempotent replay.

subject.description: Immutable subject generation allocated to the entry.

warning.description: Optional advisory that does not weaken the generation fence.

QueueEnqueueV2Response.title: QueueEnqueueV2Response

QueueEntry.description: A queue entry shape returned by list / lease.

entry_id.description:
Stable entry id (unique within the project queue). Mutation calls
target this id.

expire_after_secs.description:
Grace window in seconds after `run_at` before the entry is expired
and dropped on sweep. `None` means never expire. Ignored when
`run_at` is `None`.

run_at.description:
RFC 3339 earliest-dispatch time for a deferred entry. While `now`
is before this instant the entry is pending-but-not-leasable.
`None` for ordinary (dispatch-ASAP) entries.

subject_dispatch.description:
Full dispatch envelope — included so the daemon can lease an entry
and start work without a second roundtrip.

subject_id.description: Subject id from the dispatch envelope.

task_id.description: Task id, if this entry's subject is a built-in task.

workflow_id.description: Workflow id attached to an Assigned entry.

QueueEntry.title: QueueEntry

QueueLeaseBlock.description: A candidate intentionally not leased by the v2 scheduler.

conflicts_with.description: Existing execution that caused the conflict, when applicable.

QueueLeaseBlock.title: QueueLeaseBlock

QueueLeaseBlockReason.description: Why a v2 lease candidate was left untouched.

oneOf.description: The exact subject generation already has an active execution.
Another active execution owns the repository/head ref.

The entry has an expired assignment that must be reconciled/recovered,
never handed out as fresh work.
The stored entry lacks the identity needed for fail-closed scheduling.

QueueLeaseBlockReason.title: QueueLeaseBlockReason

QueueLeaseFence.description: Compare-and-swap identity for the queue lease currently owning a workflow.

expires_at.description:
Backend-clock expiry. Expiry makes the lease recoverable, never an
ordinary fresh-leasing candidate.

generation.description:
Positive monotonic lease generation. Recovery transfers ownership by
incrementing this value, fencing the previous daemon instance.

owner_id.description:
Daemon/scheduler instance currently authorized to renew or terminalize
the lease.

QueueLeaseMutationOutcome.description: Result category for a generation-fenced queue mutation.

oneOf.description: Mutation succeeded and the response contains the current fence.
The entry is already in the requested terminal/pending state.

Owner, lease generation, workflow generation, or subject generation did
not match. The caller has no authority to mutate the entry.
Recovery was requested before backend-clock expiry.
Entry exists but is not assigned.

QueueLeaseMutationOutcome.title: QueueLeaseMutationOutcome

QueueLeaseMutationResponse.description: Response shared by renew, recover, completion, and release-pending v2.

execution.description:
Current fence after success, including a transferred/incremented lease
generation after recovery.

QueueLeaseMutationResponse.title: QueueLeaseMutationResponse

QueueLeaseRecoverRequest.description: Request to transfer an expired lease to a new daemon owner.

execution.description:
Last durable execution fence. The backend CAS-checks its owner and lease
generation, then preserves workflow/subject generations.

ttl_secs.description: Optional requested TTL; the backend may clamp it to policy.

QueueLeaseRecoverRequest.title: QueueLeaseRecoverRequest

QueueLeaseRenewRequest.description: Request to renew an exact, still-owned lease.

ttl_secs.description: Optional requested TTL; the backend may clamp it to policy.

QueueLeaseRenewRequest.title: QueueLeaseRenewRequest

exclude_subjects.description:
Subjects to skip during lease selection.

Entries whose `subject_dispatch.subject_key()` matches any id in
this list stay in Pending status and are not returned in the
lease response. No state transition occurs for them. Hosts use
this to tell the queue "this subject already has an in-flight
workflow" so it advances past the head-of-line entry instead of
returning it for the daemon to immediately release back.
Backward-compat: `None` / omitted is identical to today's behavior.

max.description: Maximum number of entries to lease in this call.

workflow_ids.description:
Optional daemon-provided workflow ids to attach to leased entries.
If set, length MUST be exactly `max` (plugin returns an error
otherwise). If `None`, the plugin generates synthetic UUIDs.

exclude.description: Active execution fences to exclude from selection and collision checks.

max.description: Maximum number of entries to lease.

owner_id.description: Stable daemon/scheduler instance id that will own new leases.

workflow_ids.description:
Kernel-preallocated workflow ids. Length must equal `max`; a queue entry
that already owns a workflow id keeps it and does not consume a new id.

blocked.description: Candidates intentionally left in place due to a typed fence.

leased.description: Newly leased entries with complete ownership fences.

status.description: Filter by status (values from [`status`]). Empty means all.

QueueMutationResponse.description:
Generic mutation result used by hold / release / drop / mark_assigned /
completion.

changed.description:
`true` if the entry state changed. `false` if the entry was already
in the requested state (idempotent no-op) or was not found.

not_found.description: `true` if the entry was not found (idempotent on missing).

QueueMutationResponse.title: QueueMutationResponse

next_run_at.description:
Earliest future `run_at` (RFC 3339) across pending deferred entries,
or `None` when the queue holds no future-dated entries. The daemon
uses this to wake precisely at the next deferred entry's dispatch
time. Expired entries are swept before this is computed, so a value
here is always in the future relative to the plugin's clock.

entry_id.description: Entry id to return to Pending.

reason.description: Audit reason describing why the entry is being released back.

entry_id.description: Entry id whose status was changed.

QueueReleasePendingV2Request.description:
Generation-fenced return-to-pending request. The queue preserves the
canonical workflow id/generation for the next lease attempt.

reason.description: Auditable reason for returning the entry to Pending.

QueueReleasePendingV2Request.title: QueueReleasePendingV2Request

entry_ids.description:
New order (partial — entries not in this list keep their existing
position).

reordered_count.description: Count of entries whose position changed.

deferred.description:
Subset of `pending` that is deferred — `run_at` is still in the
future, so these are not yet leasable. Lets callers distinguish
"scheduled for later" from "ready to dispatch" without inspecting
every entry. `0` on backends that predate deferred dispatch.

pending.description: Pending entries (includes deferred entries not yet leasable).

RepositoryReservation.description: Repository/ref ownership reserved for one execution generation.

head_ref.description:
Fully-qualified mutable head ref owned by this run, for example
`refs/heads/animus/TASK-1175`.

repository.description:
Canonical repository identity. Hosts SHOULD use a normalized remote URL
or provider `owner/name` identity and compare it case-insensitively where
the provider does.

SubjectDispatch.description:
Full dispatch envelope handed off from queue / scheduler / trigger to the
workflow runner.

Carries the subject identity (`subject`), the workflow ref to run, and
optional input + variables + priority + trigger source + requested-at
timestamp. The shape is wire-compatible with the previous home in
ao-cli's `protocol` crate.

actor.description:
Caller identity this dispatch runs as. `None` is a system/global run
(the legacy default). Owner-scoped schedules attach a kernel-minted
[`Actor`] here (see the schedule's `owner_id`); the daemon relays it to
the workflow runner so downstream provider + plugin channels scope to
the owner. Additive and back-compat: omitted from the wire when absent.

input.description: Optional initial input JSON for workflow variables.

subject.description:
The subject this dispatch targets, or `None` for a genuinely
subjectless run — a workflow dispatched with NO bound subject (subject
template vars are simply absent downstream). Omitted from the wire when
absent; older payloads always carry a subject, so this stays
backward-tolerant on deserialize.

trigger_source.description:
Tag identifying which subsystem produced this dispatch
(e.g., `"ready-queue"`, `"trigger:slack"`, `"schedule:nightly"`).

SubjectGeneration.description: A canonical subject identity and the immutable generation being executed.

generation.description:
Positive backend/queue generation. A later generation cannot be
satisfied by work or proof from an earlier one.

SubjectId.description:
Backend-qualified identifier for a subject.

Convention is `"<backend>:<native_id>"`, e.g. `"linear:ENG-123"`,
`"jira:PROJ-456"`, `"github:owner/repo#789"`, `"native:TASK-001"`. The
daemon treats the value as opaque; only the originating backend
interprets the native portion.

The `backend:` prefix is reserved. Plugin authors should always emit
prefixed ids so cross-backend collisions are impossible.

SubjectRef.description: Backend-qualified subject reference with optional display metadata.
